text: The flow data covers 2026-06-10 05:00 to 2026-10-01 00:45 at 15-minute grain for 167 stations on the lines U1, U2, U3, U5, U6, U7, U8, U9 (there is no U4 data). Dates outside this window cannot be answered from data; only clearly labelled scenarios are possible.

There is NO platform-capacity, headway, timetable or train-load data. 'Safe platform capacity' therefore cannot be measured or quoted; answers must say so and use a relative proxy (each station's own busiest-5% level, or predicted load) instead.

The events file has 457 events (182 with a venue name) from 2026-06-10 to 2026-09-30. Events carry a venue name and address but NO station key or coordinates, and attendance is an organiser estimate. The file contains 4 InnoTrans/Messe events.
The passenger flows are simulated. 17711 readings equal exactly 500 (a clipping artefact, 1.2% of readings) although values up to 3000 exist.

There are 30 recorded closures (reasons: safety inspection x10, switch replacement x7, track maintenance x6, signal upgrades x4, power system maintenance x3). They are simulated maintenance closures; closed stations read 0 and neighbouring stations show no measurable extra load.
The data has no origin-destination flows or route choices: which alternative routes passengers prefer, and why two stations are coupled, cannot be measured — only suggested.
How many passengers divert around a closure, and to which stations, is ASSUMED (diversion shares 25/50/75 %, nearest open stations). Closure pressure is a model-based scenario, never a measurement.
The events file names the arena 'Uber Arena'; operators may say 'Mercedes-Benz Arena' (its earlier name). They are treated as the same venue — an assumption to be stated.
Energy is daily MWh per line only; there is no rolling-stock, timetable or route-length data, so energy explanations are limited to ridership evidence.
A new dataset (2026-09-22 to 2026-10-01) is provided on the final day; loaders merge every matching file (dedupe on timestamp) and coverage is read from the data.

text: Rudow: weekday commute peak at 18:00 with 223.2 passengers per 15 min; the mean of all stations' own weekday peaks is 265.8; Rudow does not exceed it.

Highest weekday hourly-average flows per 15 min: Kurfürstendamm 835 (peak 18:00); Spichernstr. 834 (peak 17:00); Berliner Str. 770 (peak 7:00); Wittenbergplatz 763 (peak 17:00); Zoologischer Garten Bhf 731 (peak 18:00).

Energy per passenger (Wh, total daily MWh / passengers at the line's stations): U5 546; U6 521; U8 484; U7 427; U3 326; U1 258; U2 256; U9 253. Worst: U5 (546 Wh), best: U9 (253 Wh). Passengers are approximated per line (interchanges count on every line they serve).

Stations whose closure fragments the network most (passengers affected per day = own + cut-off stations): Alexanderplatz Bhf 181565 (25 stations cut off, 3 parts); Bismarckstr. 135127 (18 stations cut off, 3 parts); Schillingstr. 132553 (18 stations cut off, 2 parts); Strausberger Platz 125632 (17 stations cut off, 2 parts); Weberwiese 118800 (16 stations cut off, 2 parts). Trains are assumed not to run through a closed station.

Uber Arena: 18 events in the data (median attendance 1765). In the hour after they end the flow is, versus the same weekday hour in neighbouring weeks, Warschauer Str. x6.5; Schlesisches Tor x6.2; Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz x2.0; Hermannplatz x1.3. The event effect is local to the 1-2 stations next to the venue.
Rain (> 0.5 mm per 15 min, 419 slots) lifts total network flow to x1.27 of the dry value for the same weekday and time, and the number of stations pinned at 500 rises from 1.9 to 2.9 per slot.

Hermannplatz is served by U7 and U8. Its direct neighbours are Boddinstr., Rathaus Neukölln, Schönleinstr., Südstern. No U8 station is named Neukölln: Rathaus Neukölln and Neukölln are U7 stations, so 'U8 between Hermannplatz and Neukölln' does not exist as such in the network data.

Ranking stations by the predicted busy-slot LOAD has skill: over 8 replay days the predicted top-3 stations had a mean observed peak of 1671 per 15 min versus 529 for the average station, Spearman 0.44. Ranking by the probability of exceeding a station's own p95 has NO skill (Spearman -0.05): those exceedances are noise-driven. Load, not p95-exceedance, is the ranking to use.

TabPFN demand model on held-out days: MAE 74.62 vs 77.87 for the naive station-slot mean, RMSE 135.61 vs 135.05; pinball-loss skill +0.5%. It adds context-conditioned probabilities more than a different decision.
